body:
Meaning and applications of fintech

Fintech means the use of digital technology to provide or improve financial services. It includes electronic payments, digital banking, technology-supported insurance, online investment services and certain methods of verifying customers or detecting suspicious transactions.

Fintech is not the same as manufacturing electronic equipment. A mobile payment application uses software, communication networks and banking infrastructure, even though the phone itself contains semiconductor devices.

GIFT City and international financial services

GIFT City stands for Gujarat International Finance Tec-City. It is located near Gandhinagar in Gujarat.

GIFT City is home to the GIFT International Financial Services Centre (IFSC), India's first international financial services centre. An IFSC is a designated location intended for specified financial activities with an international orientation under the applicable regulatory framework.

Activities in an IFSC may include international banking, capital-market services, fund management, insurance and other permitted financial services. The presence of an IFSC does not mean that all financial transactions taking place anywhere in Gujarat fall under its regulatory framework.

IFSCA: the IFSC regulator

The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) was established on 27 April 2020 under the International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019.

Its headquarters are at GIFT City, Gandhinagar. It acts as a unified authority for the development and regulation of financial products, financial services and financial institutions in India's IFSCs.

Before IFSCA was established, different financial-sector regulators were responsible for relevant IFSC activities within their respective fields. IFSCA provides a unified regulatory framework for the IFSC. The ordinary domestic financial sector outside the IFSC continues to be governed by the applicable domestic authorities and laws.

GIFT City is the location and financial-services ecosystem; IFSCA is the statutory regulator of activities within the IFSC.

UPI: a national digital payment system

Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is a system developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) to facilitate electronic payments between participating bank accounts through compatible applications.

UPI was launched in its pilot form on 11 April 2016. It allows payment services to work across participating banks and applications, subject to the applicable requirements.

For example, a customer in Ahmedabad may scan a merchant's payment QR code, review the intended recipient and amount, and authorise a payment through a UPI application. The actual payment service uses the national UPI arrangement and participating financial institutions.

A UPI transaction and a government-service application are separate processes. A state portal may offer online payment methods, potentially including UPI where integrated, but the portal is not the creator of UPI.

Fintech innovation and regulatory sandboxes

A regulatory sandbox is a controlled arrangement in which an eligible entity may test an innovative financial product or service under specified conditions and regulatory supervision.

IFSCA introduced the FinTech Sandbox Framework, 2026, effective from 16 March 2026. It provides arrangements for different forms of controlled fintech testing within the relevant regulatory framework.

A sandbox is not permission to conduct every financial activity without rules. Participation, testing conditions and any regulatory relief are determined under the applicable framework.

Separating the institutions and technologies

NameWhat it isMain association
GIFT CityFinancial and business locationGandhinagar, Gujarat
GIFT IFSCInternational financial-services jurisdictionPermitted international financial activities
IFSCAStatutory regulatorDevelopment and regulation of IFSC activities
NPCINational payments organisationDevelopment of UPI and other payment systems
UPIDigital payment interfaceInteroperable payments through participating banks

Prelims focus

  • GIFT City stands for Gujarat International Finance Tec-City and is near Gandhinagar.
  • GIFT IFSC is India's first international financial services centre.
  • IFSCA was established on 27 April 2020 under the IFSCA Act, 2019.
  • NPCI developed UPI; its pilot launch took place on 11 April 2016.
  • The IFSCA FinTech Sandbox Framework, 2026 took effect on 16 March 2026.
  • Trap: UPI is a national payment system, not a payment system created by GIFT City or IFSCA.

[International Financial Services Centres Authority, About Us, Establishment and Role; International Financial Services Centres Authority, FinTech Sandbox Framework, 2026, FAQs, effective date and framework overview; National Payments Corporation of India, UPI Launch Press Release, 11 April 2016; NPCI, UPI Product Booklet, Background and Launch History; Gujarat Informatics Limited, Digital Gujarat Portal, online payment features; consulted 5 November 2026.]

body:
Why a technology ecosystem requires different skills

Digital government services, semiconductor factories, electronics manufacturing and fintech do not employ only one kind of worker. Their activities require different combinations of technical, administrative and practical skills.

A software professional who develops an online application does different work from a technician who tests a packaged chip. Both may contribute to the same wider technology ecosystem.

Major categories of work

ActivityTypical workRelevant skills
Digital public servicesApplication development, records, assisted service deliverySoftware, administration, digital literacy
Semiconductor designDesigning and checking electronic circuitsElectronics, computing, design tools
Wafer fabricationOperating and maintaining fabrication facilitiesTechnical operations, process awareness, safety
ATMP and OSATAssembly, equipment operation, testing and quality checksElectronics, equipment handling, quality assurance
Electronics manufacturingProducing components and assembling electronic systemsProduction, inspection, equipment maintenance
FintechFinancial software, transaction support, risk monitoringComputing, financial knowledge, cybersecurity

Technicians, operators, engineers, software developers and service workers all have important roles. A major semiconductor investment can also create demand for supporting services such as maintenance, transport and facilities management.

Chips to Startup: national semiconductor-design skills

The Chips to Startup (C2S) Programme is a national initiative intended to strengthen India's semiconductor design skills and educational capacity.

It aims to generate 85,000 industry-ready professionals at various higher-education levels in semiconductor chip design.

According to a Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology release dated 14 August 2026, more than 68,000 students had been trained under the programme by that reporting date, and 332 academic institutions had been provided access to electronic design automation tools.

Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools are computer-based tools that assist in designing and checking electronic circuits. Access to design tools helps students learn chip design, but does not mean that every participating institution operates a commercial semiconductor fab.

The 85,000 figure is the programme's target. More than 68,000 is a reported achievement as of 14 August 2026. Both figures concern the national programme, not only students from Gujarat.

FutureSkills PRIME and wider digital skills

FutureSkills PRIME is a national skilling initiative of MeitY and NASSCOM. It supports training, reskilling and upskilling in emerging technologies.

Its fields include areas such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, cybersecurity, data analytics and the Internet of Things.

Reskilling means learning skills for a different role, while upskilling means improving or extending skills relevant to an existing area of work.

These skills can support government digital systems, industrial applications, software companies and financial technology services.

Gujarat's semiconductor ATMP training initiative

A Gujarat Department of Science and Technology government resolution dated 23 September 2024 describes a semiconductor ATMP training initiative at Pandit Deendayal Energy University (PDEU), developed in cooperation with Micron Technology and the state department.

The planned training centre is connected with the workforce needs of Micron's Sanand semiconductor facility. Its training focus includes operators, technicians and engineers.

The resolution records Micron's commitment to send 1,000 employees for training over 5 years. This is a planned training commitment stated in the 2024 document, not a verified count of employees who had completed training by November 2026.

The initiative illustrates the connection between an industrial investment and a local educational institution. A semiconductor factory needs workers who can operate equipment safely, inspect output, follow procedures and maintain quality.

Connecting Gujarat's technology activities

The Gujarat ecosystem can be understood through 4 related functions:

  • Service delivery: Digital Gujarat, e-Gram, Digital Seva Setu, e-Dhara and other portals help citizens and departments use information electronically.
  • Industrial production: semiconductor and electronics projects at Sanand, Dholera and Surat support the manufacture and preparation of electronic devices.
  • Financial services: GIFT IFSC and IFSCA support the international financial-services ecosystem, while UPI is a national system used for digital payments throughout Gujarat.
  • Workforce development: national initiatives such as C2S and FutureSkills PRIME, together with state and industry-supported training, prepare people for different technology-related roles.

Communication networks and computing infrastructure support many of these activities. Industrial policy, training and business investment influence how rapidly an ecosystem can develop.

How to solve statement-based questions

For questions about Gujarat's digital and electronics ecosystem, begin by identifying the function being described. A statement about maintaining land records points towards e-Dhara, while one about providing village-level access points towards e-Gram. A statement about connecting government offices points towards GSWAN, while one about shared hosting points towards GSDC.

For semiconductor projects, check the location, activity and status separately. Dholera's Tata–PSMC project concerns wafer fabrication, while the major Sanand projects include assembly and testing. Approval, planned capacity and commercial production must not be treated as interchangeable facts.

For fintech, distinguish a payment system from a financial regulator. UPI is associated with NPCI; IFSC regulation is associated with IFSCA.

Prelims focus

  • C2S aims to develop 85,000 industry-ready semiconductor-design professionals nationally.
  • MeitY reported more than 68,000 C2S students trained as of 14 August 2026.
  • FutureSkills PRIME is a MeitY–NASSCOM initiative for emerging-technology skills.
  • The Gujarat government resolution dated 23 September 2024 describes an ATMP training initiative at PDEU with Micron.
  • The PDEU–Micron training commitment was 1,000 employees over 5 years, not 1,000 already verified as trained.
  • Trap: Employment projections, training targets and reported achievements are different measures.

[Press Information Bureau, Chips to Start-ups Programme Strengthens India's Semiconductor Design Ecosystem and Industry-Ready Talent, 14 August 2026; Press Information Bureau, FutureSkills PRIME Strengthens India's Future-Ready Digital Workforce, 14 August 2026; Department of Science and Technology, Government of Gujarat, Semiconductor ATMP Training Centre at PDEU, Government Resolution approved 23 September 2024, Section 3 and Training Schedule; Gujarat State Electronics Mission, Overview; Press Information Bureau, SEMICON India 2026, 17–19 September 2026; consulted 5 November 2026.]
